objective: Record a voucher payment reminder only after the internal email service proves provider acceptance, make retries safe across lost responses and post-acceptance crashes using a stable provider idempotency key, and expose failures in the cron result without replaying historical reminders.
current_evidence: cleanupAbandonedVouchers marks payment_reminder_sent_at and increments sent after any resolved fetch, including 401, 429, 5xx, or a 200 body with ok:false.
A lost response or crash after Resend acceptance leaves the marker null and causes a duplicate retry because send-email supplies no provider idempotency key.
The hold-expiry sibling also ignores the response and logs SENT; it has no durable retry state after the hold is expired.

corrections: Persist and reuse the exact provider payload so mutable branding or a transient branding lookup failure cannot change a retry under the same idempotency key.
Recheck voucher age immediately before each sequential send so a batch cannot cross the 24-hour deletion boundary.
Require a non-empty string provider ID at both the provider and internal-email acceptance boundaries.

behavior_to_preserve: Only PENDING vouchers between 15 minutes and 24 hours old receive the one-time payment-link reminder.
Tenant branding, recipient, amount, and original payment URL remain unchanged.
Pending vouchers are deleted by the existing 24-hour cleanup policy; no historical reminder is replayed.
Other service and administrator email types retain their existing behavior.
forbidden_behavior: Marking a reminder after transport rejection, non-2xx, malformed response, or ok:false
Duplicate provider sends after an unknown outcome or database-stamp failure
Sending a reminder for a voucher already eligible for deletion
acceptance_tests: 401, 429, 5xx, 200 ok:false, malformed responses, and network failures leave the reminder marker null and surface a failure.
A provider-accepted response stamps exactly the same tenant-owned PENDING voucher and reports accepted, not delivered.
A database-stamp failure retries with the identical provider key and payload; the later successful attempt stamps once.
Only a verified service caller can cause send-email to attach the derived voucher reminder Idempotency-Key.
Expired vouchers are deleted without receiving a new reminder.
The internal cron-to-email request has a bounded timeout; an unknown outcome remains retryable under the same provider key.
A retry after mutable tenant branding or a transient branding-query failure reuses the first persisted provider payload.
A sequential batch that crosses the deletion boundary skips the now-expiring voucher before provider submission.
Non-string and blank provider IDs are rejected at the provider and internal-email boundaries.
The existing message boundary, voucher checkout, Edge, TypeScript, and build checks remain green.
existing_customer_cases: No voucher ID, balance, status, buyer, recipient, payment URL, or commercial setting changes.
No historical reminder marker is cleared or replayed.
scope_limitations: The additive durable-intent migration is locally exercised only; its target ledger must be verified before deployment.

The sibling hold-expiry path now reports provider acceptance or failure and uses the durable intent, but it still lacks rediscovery after the hold has expired. COR-04 remains open for that queue/claim design.
Provider behavior is simulated; no genuine email was sent and provider acceptance is not delivery.
migration_order: Verify the target migration ledger, then apply 20260920085900_durable_payment_reminder_email_intents.sql before deploying either Edge Function.

The migration sorts before the locked 20260920090000 pricing migration so an untouched target can stop before that unapproved commercial change; an environment where 20260920090000 is already recorded requires explicit ledger reconciliation.
rollback_strategy: Roll back the Edge Function source while leaving the additive intent schema in place until a separately reviewed migration can remove it. Keep existing reminder markers and customer/payment data; never mass resend.
